what_this_arm_is: G1's SELECTION RULE applied to THIS corpus: the LARGEST-AREA `traffic sign` detection per clip, 32 clips drawn at random from the 62 that carry one. Rendered TWICE — once under G1's own protocol (tight box crop, 4x LANCZOS, from the 448-px bridge) and once under this study's (6x-box context window from native 640) — so the SELECTION effect and the RENDERING effect are separated rather than confounded.
adjudication_basis: BOTH renderings of each detection were viewed before the verdict was fixed. That is deliberately the best available evidence rather than a single protocol; where the two disagreed it is recorded below, because the disagreement is itself the measurement.

g1_subclass_1_empty_box.definition: G1_RESULT.md's own first subclass — `no sign visible in the crop at all: sky, foliage, building walls, clouds`. This is the quantity its ~two-thirds figure counts, so it is scored separately here rather than folded into `wrong`.
g1_subclass_1_empty_box.note: ZERO of the 32 max-area crops are empty. Both `wrong` calls contain a real, salient object that is simply not a traffic sign.

notes.1000: ⭐ THE RENDERING DISAGREED WITH ITSELF, and G1's protocol WON. The context crop showed a tall narrow strip that read as a bollard (I had it `unclear`); the tight 4x crop shows a yellow diamond priority sign on its post unmistakably. The box is very tall and thin, so the 6x-context window shrank the sign to nothing. ⇒ a context crop is not uniformly better, and the G1 protocol is NOT the cause of G1's empties.
notes.1001: a GREEN TRAFFIC LIGHT detected as `traffic sign`. A genuine cross-class confusion inside the traffic-infrastructure family — and the failure mode that matters most for a KIND-blind consumer, because `ph1_fuse.py` counts generic `traffic sign` tracks without checking what kind of sign it is.
notes.1003: an illuminated commercial sign reading `GLOST` at night, on a dark rural road. Sign-shaped, sign-mounted, not a traffic sign. Same family as #207 (a pharmacy cross) and #210 (an advertising hoarding) in the uniform sample.
notes.1013_1018_1022_1024_1026: unresolvable at this pixel scale under BOTH renderings.
